about: One entry per route. Every route starts in Tokyo (Narita NRT or Haneda HND both count), is a round trip, and is tracked in business and first class. Rules are Dan's own words unless marked. Later sessions add tactics and more routes here.

tactics.move: Fly ZIPAIR ZG16 from Narita in its lie-flat "ZIP Full-Flat" seat.
tactics.why: ZIPAIR is Japan Airlines' low-cost airline; its 18 lie-flat seats launched at ¥188,500 one way, well under full-service business, and it has been the cheapest nonstop business in our captures ($3,711–3,912 round trip against $5,643–5,791 on United or ANA) (our data: LEARNING.md).

It flies only a few days a week (three a week through 2 Jan 2027, one to three a week in January 2027), and on other days the cheapest nonstop is United or ANA at about $1,900 more (our data: LEARNING.md).

tactics.move: Price ZIPAIR one way and fly another airline the other way.
tactics.why: ZIPAIR sells each direction as its own one-way fare, so its cheap leg can be paired with a different return.

tactics.move: On United UA6, buy Premium Plus and upgrade to Polaris with PlusPoints (not on a Basic Polaris or Premium Plus fare).
tactics.why: A paid Premium Plus ticket upgrades to Polaris for 30 PlusPoints, for United elite members; United's new 787-9 on this route has 35 Premium Plus seats.

tactics.move: Price one-stop business against Delta's Haneda nonstop.
tactics.why: In our captures the cheapest one-stop business was about $370 less than Delta DL274.

tactics.move: Ask a Tokyo discount agency for Air Canada business.
tactics.why: Inter Resort lists Air Canada business to Detroit from ¥454,000 round trip on its discount-fare list (see BROKERS.md).

tactics.move: On Delta, buy a lower cabin and upgrade to Delta One with miles through Delta Reservations.
tactics.why: Delta says Reservations can upgrade a purchased ticket to Delta One with miles; which fares on the Tokyo route qualify is not stated.

rules: A nonstop exists and is always shown first on its own line: El Al, Tel Aviv-Narita, twice weekly, 787-8 with 20 business seats (japanaviationhub.com/?p=1221, read 2 Nov 2026); confirm the current frequency from the data source.
Stopovers on the way (a Europe stop, or a Europe trip with Tel Aviv folded in) are welcome as alternatives, never as the first line.

sources.note: Etihad sale 3-7 May 2026, Narita-Tel Aviv business JPY 547,810; one publisher only, so no line
Etihad sale 23-27 Aug 2026, Narita-Tel Aviv business JPY 720,420; same publisher as above, so no line

tactics.move: Price one-stop business against El Al's Narita nonstop.
tactics.why: In our captures the cheapest one-stop business ($4,511, Thai Airways with El Al via Bangkok) was $780 less than El Al's nonstop.

tactics.move: Fold Tel Aviv into a Europe trip: a sale business fare to a European city plus a separate ticket on to Tel Aviv.
tactics.why: In Etihad's August 2026 Japan sale, Narita–Tel Aviv business was ¥720,420 against ¥466,350 to Milan or ¥490,560 to Madrid; the Europe–Tel Aviv leg is not priced here.

tactics.move: If flying Etihad, buy in its sales and take the free Abu Dhabi stopover.
tactics.why: Etihad's Japan sale fares include Narita–Tel Aviv and qualify for its Abu Dhabi stopover programme, with up to 2 free hotel nights depending on the flight.

tactics.move: Buy Etihad business in its Japan sales.
tactics.why: Etihad runs Narita business sales every month or two (Barcelona ¥353,090 in June 2026, ¥552,160 in its 8–15 Nov 2026 sale).

tactics.move: Price Madrid, Milan or Lisbon against Barcelona and take the train or a short flight on.
tactics.why: In Etihad's 8–15 Nov 2026 sale Narita business was ¥516,450 to Madrid, ¥470,960 to Milan and ¥473,100 to Lisbon, against ¥552,160 to Barcelona.

tactics.move: On Etihad, take the free Abu Dhabi stopover.
tactics.why: Etihad's Japan sale fares qualify for its Abu Dhabi stopover programme, with up to 2 free hotel nights depending on the flight.

tactics.move: On Turkish Airlines via Istanbul, claim the free Stopover hotel.
tactics.why: Business passengers get free hotel nights in Istanbul on a stop of 20 hours or more, with an extra night for long-haul trips from Japan.
